verses.text: They crossed the sea and arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.
As Jesus stepped out of the boat, a man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs to meet him.
The man lived among the tombs. Nobody could keep him tied up—not even with chains.
They’d often chained his hands and feet, but he snapped the chains and smashed the shackles. Nobody was strong enough to control him.
Night and day, among the tombs and on the hills, he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones. 💔
When he saw Jesus from far away, he ran over and bowed down in front of him.
He shouted loudly, “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Swear by God you won’t torment me!”
For Jesus had already told him, “You unclean spirit, come out of the man!”
Jesus asked him, “What’s your name?” He answered, “My name is Legion, because there are many of us.”
The spirits kept begging Jesus not to send them out of that region.
A huge herd of pigs was feeding on the hillside nearby.
The spirits begged him, “Send us into the pigs. Let us go into them.”
Jesus let them. The unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs. The whole herd—about two thousand—rushed down the steep slope into the sea and drowned. 🐖
The pig herders ran off and told the story in town and out in the countryside. People came to see what had happened.
They came to Jesus and saw the man who’d been controlled by the legion sitting there, dressed and in his right mind. They were scared.
The people who had seen it told them what happened to the possessed man and the pigs.
Then the people began begging Jesus to leave their region.
As Jesus got into the boat, the man who’d been possessed begged to go with him.
Jesus didn’t let him. He said, “Go home to your people. Tell them everything the Lord has done for you and how he showed you mercy.”
The man went off and began telling the story throughout the Decapolis—everything Jesus had done for him. Everyone was amazed.
Jesus crossed back over to the other side, and a large crowd gathered around him by the sea.
One of the synagogue leaders, Jairus, came over. When he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet
and begged him earnestly: “My little daughter is close to dying. Please come lay your hands on her so she can be healed and live.”
Jesus went with him. A huge crowd followed and pressed in around him.
A woman in the crowd had been bleeding for twelve years.
She’d suffered a lot under many doctors and spent everything she had. Nothing helped; she was only getting worse.
She’d heard about Jesus, so she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
She was saying to herself, “If I can just touch his clothes, I’ll be healed.”
Right away, the bleeding stopped, and she felt in her body that she was healed from her suffering.
Jesus immediately realized power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
His disciples said, “You see this crowd pressing in on you, and you’re asking, ‘Who touched me?’”
But Jesus kept looking around to see who had done it.
The woman, knowing what had happened to her, came trembling with fear. She fell down in front of him and told him the whole truth.
Jesus told her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace; you’re healed from your suffering.”
While he was still speaking, some people came from the synagogue leader’s house: “Your daughter has died. Why bother the teacher anymore?”
Jesus heard their message and told the synagogue leader, “Don’t be afraid. Just believe.”
He didn’t let anyone follow him except Peter, James, and James’s brother John.
They arrived at the synagogue leader’s house. Jesus saw all the commotion—people crying and wailing loudly.
He went inside and told them, “Why all this crying and commotion? The child isn’t dead; she’s asleep.”
They laughed at him. But Jesus sent them all outside, then took the child’s father and mother and the disciples with him into the room where she was.
He took the girl by the hand and said, “Talitha cumi,” which means, “Little girl, I’m telling you: get up!”
Right away, the girl got up and started walking around. She was twelve years old. They were completely stunned.
Jesus firmly told them not to let anyone know about this. Then he said to give her something to eat.
